extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer-review researchers, clinical trialists, and developers of peer-review/reporting tools
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating completeness of reporting in two-arm parallel-group randomized controlled trial (RCT) manuscripts using CONSORT-based criteria (COBPeer) versus the usual journal peer-review process, and measuring diagnostic accuracy against systematic-reviewer reference standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadequate reporting (overall definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inadequate reporting was defined as incomplete reporting or a switch in primary outcome and considered nine domains: the eight most important CONSORT domains and a switch in primary outcome(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the target condition for the diagnostic comparison; the nine domains form the unit of assessment (scale 0–9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes (CONSORT item 6a)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For COBPeer: item elicited via bullet points extracted from the CONSORT Explanation & Elaboration; ECRs indicate for each bullet point whether requested information was completely reported (yes/no). A domain is considered incompletely reported if information for at least one bullet point is missing. Reference standard: systematic reviewers used the CONSORT checklist and rated the domain as 'completely reported', 'partially reported', or 'not reported' and considered 'partially' or 'not reported' as incompletely reported (only if it was a real barrier to conduct a systematic review). Usual peer-review: domain rated as incompletely reported if at least one peer reviewer raised concerns; in disagreement, rated as incompletely reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomization / sequence generation (CONSORT item 8a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of reporting of random sequence generation (item 8a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COBPeer elicits specific bullet points from CONSORT E&E; same rule: any missing bullet → domain considered incompletely reported. Reference standard and usual peer-review combination rules as above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation concealment mechanism (CONSORT item 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of reporting of allocation concealment mechanism (item 9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COBPeer requires yes/no for each bullet point derived from CONSORT E&E; domain considered incompletely reported if at least one bullet missing. Reference standard rates 'partially' or 'not reported' as incompletely reported when it hinders systematic review. Usual peer-review: flagged by any reviewer → incompletely reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding (CONSORT items 11a, 11b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of reporting regarding blinding (items 11a and 11b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When blinding was not possible, the related domain (item 11a/b) was rated 'no incomplete reporting' in the study's primary outcome metric. COBPeer and reference-standard rules on bullet points and partial/not reported apply. Usual peer-review: any reviewer raising concern results in domain rated incompletely reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant flow (CONSORT items 13a, 13b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of participant flow reporting (items 13a and 13b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COBPeer: assess bullet points; any missing information → domain incomplete. Reference standard required that incompleteness be a real barrier to conducting a systematic review. Note: participant flow was identified in training as one of the least accurately evaluated domains by ECRs (contextual performance info).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes and estimation (CONSORT item 17a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the reporting of outcomes and their estimation (item 17a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COBPeer uses CONSORT E&E–derived bullet points for yes/no checks; domain incomplete if any bullet missing. Reference-standard and usual peer-review combination rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harms (CONSORT item 19)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COBPeer elicits explicit bullet points for harms reporting; domain considered incompletely reported if at least one bullet point was missing. Reference standard judged incompleteness only when it impeded systematic-review extraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial registration (CONSORT item 23)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COBPeer requires verification of registration details via bullet points; ECRs indicated completeness per bullet. In training this domain was uniformly well-evaluated. Reference standard and usual peer-review rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Switch in primary outcome(s) (detection rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A switch in primary outcome was defined as a primary outcome added, deleted, or changed between the primary outcome(s) published in the protocol or register and the primary outcome(s) reported in the report. Discrepancies in definition (variable of interest, time frame, metric) were considered a switch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COBPeer process: ECRs compare primary outcome(s) in manuscript to trial register (based on COMPare process) and indicate 'no switch', 'presence of a switch', or 'unable to assess' (not registered or insufficiently defined). Reference standard categories included 'no switch', 'presence of a switch', 'not available' (not registered), or 'unable to assess'. Usual peer-review: domain rated as presence of switch if any peer reviewer flagged it.

rubrics_metrics.name: COBPeer item-level elicitation and domain decision rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For CONSORT domains, COBPeer elicits specific bullet points extracted from the CONSORT Explanation & Elaboration and asks ECRs to indicate for each bullet point whether the requested information was completely reported (yes/no).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A domain was considered incompletely reported if information for at least one bullet point was missing. For the 'switched primary outcome' domain, the tool offered 'no switch', 'presence of a switch', or 'unable to assess'. After assessment, COBPeer automatically generates a standardized and individualized peer-review report detailing missing information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training module requirement for ECRs
rubrics_metrics.description: ECRs had to complete an online training module before using COBPeer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The module begins with a reminder about importance of assessing completeness and switched outcomes, then describes each item and bullet points. ECRs complete assessments of two extracts per domain using the tool and receive personalized feedback with explanations. In the study, ECRs were asked to perform the manuscript assessment within 30 minutes (duration not strictly monitored). Performance during training (percentage correct) was recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECR eligibility and blinding requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: ECRs were early-stage researchers (Masters, PhD students, residents, clinicians involved in research) who had never peer reviewed an RCT manuscript previously, and were blinded to journal, author names, study title, aim of the study, reference standard, and peer reviewers' comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection of ECRs targeted those with little or no prior RCT peer-review experience to evaluate feasibility of task-shifting simple reporting checks to junior reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usual peer-review process rating aggregation rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For the usual journal peer-review process, all peer-review reports from the first round were retrieved and combined; the domain was rated as 'incompletely reported' or 'presence of switch' if at least one peer reviewer rated it as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case of disagreement between peer reviewers (one raising concerns and one not), the domain was conservatively rated as 'incompletely reported' or 'presence of switch'. Two senior epidemiologists extracted data using a standardized form and achieved consensus for discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference standard assessment rules (systematic reviewers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference standard was assessment by systematic reviewers using the CONSORT checklist; each domain was rated 'completely reported', 'partially reported', or 'not reported'. A domain was considered incompletely reported if rated 'partially reported' or 'not reported'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic reviewers were instructed to rate domains as incompletely reported only if the reporting was a real barrier to conducting a systematic review; they were blinded to peer-reviewer and ECR assessments. Disagreements resolved by discussion and arbitrator if necessary. For false positives, systematic reviewers could recheck blinded to whether the false positive was identified by ECRs or usual peer-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary outcome (scoring metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary outcome: the mean number of domains accurately classified per manuscript initially submitted to the journal on a scale from 0 to 9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each of the eight CONSORT domains was rated incompletely reported (yes/no); blinding domain handled as described (if blinding not possible, related domain rated 'no incomplete reporting'); switch primary outcome rated yes/no or 'unable to assess/unavailable'. Secondary outcomes included mean number of CONSORT domains accurately classified and sensitivity/specificity/likelihood ratios to detect incompleteness and switches.
